hook.text: Why does every movie theater smell like popcorn? Funny thing is, it wasn't always welcome.

ancient.text: People have popped corn for thousands of years. In Peru, archaeologists found popcorn about six thousand seven hundred years old.

cretors.text: In eighteen eighty-five, Charles Cretors of Chicago built a steam-powered popcorn machine. Now vendors could pop it anywhere.

ban.text: But the grand movie palaces kept it out. They had fancy carpets, and silent films meant reading title cards. They wanted a classy crowd.

talkies.text: Then, in nineteen twenty-seven, the talkies arrived, and everyone came to the movies.

crash.text: When the Depression hit, a bag of popcorn cost a nickel or a dime. Theaters that started selling it stayed in business.

war.text: In World War Two, sugar rationing made candy scarce. Americans ate three times as much popcorn.

today.text: Today, a bucket costs the theater pennies to make, and it helps keep the lights on.

outro.text: So popcorn didn't sneak into the movies. It saved them.
